🔴 Valid Llama 3.1 tool-calling chats now get HTTP 400 naming role 'assistant' when an assistant turn has both text and `tool_calls`. Before this change those requests returned 200. The template names only `system`, `tool` and `ipython`, so `assistant` and `user` become suspects. Its `tool_calls` branch deliberately omits `content`, so the text probe at rendered_roles.py:645 misses the token and rejects the turn. Fix: reject only when a turn adds nothing to the prompt (no text token, no stamped tool-call name, no structural change). Alternatively, never treat roles the template emits via `message['role']` (user/assistant) as suspects.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Llama 3.1 JSON tool template (examples/tool_chat_template_llama3.1_json.jinja) has role compares only at lines 21, 81 and 104, so roles_rendered_by_chat_template returns {'system','ipython','tool'}. It renders user and assistant turns by printing `message['role']` at line 82. A /v1/chat/completions request goes through safe_apply_chat_template (vllm/renderers/hf.py:845). If it carries an assistant message with non-empty `content` plus one `tool_calls` entry (common for agent frameworks: "Let me check" + call), that message is a text suspect. assert_chat_template_rendered_messages appends a probe token to its content. The template's `elif 'tool_calls' in message` branch (lines 93-103) prints only the tool call, so the token is absent at rendered_roles.py:645. _unrendered_role_error then raises VLLMValidationError naming 'assistant', which is HTTP 400. On base the template drops that text by design and the request returns 200. Separately, every request on such templates pays at least one extra full template render because ordinary user/assistant turns count as suspects.

**Verification:** The template's `{%- elif 'tool_calls' in message %}` branch (template lines 93-103) emits only the header and the tool-call JSON, never `message['content']`. So the token is missing, and rendered_roles.py:645 returns ['assistant']. `_unrendered_role_error(['assistant'])` raises VLLMValidationError (HTTP 400). On the base branch the same request rendered and returned 200.

</details>

+    of them was omitted. If the prompt changes, tool-call names are stamped
+    and checked in a second render so messages the template actually prints
+    are cleared together. Only a mixed remainder is split, and a fully
+    omitted subgroup is still decided by one render.
+
+    When ``strip_payload`` is true, tool calls and multimodal parts are
+    removed but the message stays at the same index. That catches a tool
+    call dropped beside echoed text, and keeps neighbor lookups stable.
+    When false, the whole message is removed. The text-probe fallback uses
+    that to see whether the turn itself was omitted.
+    """
+    try:
+        baseline = render_text(conversation)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not re-render the conversation to check dropped roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return []
+    if not isinstance(baseline, str):
+        logger.warning_once(
+            "Chat template probe did not return text; skipping the dropped-role check."
+        )
+        return []
+
+    group = list(suspects)
+    if not group:
+        return []
+
+    def without(indexes: set[int]) -> list[Mapping[str, Any]]:
+        if strip_payload:
+            return _messages_without_structural_payload(conversation, indexes)
+        return _messages_without(conversation, indexes)
+
+    def dropped_in(
+        subgroup: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+        known_alternate: str | None = None,
+        *,
+        have_known: bool = False,
+    ) -> list[str]:
+        if not subgroup:
+            return []
+        if have_known:
+            alternate = known_alternate
+        else:
+            alternate = _render_probe_text(
+                render_text,
+                without({index for index, _role in subgroup}),
+            )
+        if isinstance(alternate, str) and alternate == baseline:
+            return [role for _index, role in subgroup]
+        # One comparison cannot tell which member of a changed group was
+        # the one that contributed. A single message that changes the
+        # prompt, or whose removal fails to render, is not a silent drop.
+        if len(subgroup) == 1:
+            return []
+        mid = len(subgroup) // 2
+        return dropped_in(subgroup[:mid]) + dropped_in(subgroup[mid:])
+
+    alternate = _render_probe_text(
+        render_text,
+        without({index for index, _role in group}),
+    )
+    if isinstance(alternate, str) and alternate == baseline:
+        return [role for _index, role in group]
+
+    has_tool_calls = False
+    for index, _role in group:
+        message = conversation[index]
+        tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls") if isinstance(message, Mapping) else None
+        if isinstance(tool_calls, list) and tool_calls:
+            has_tool_calls = True
+            break

+        echoed = _tool_call_indexes_echoed(conversation, group, render_text)
+        if echoed:
+            group = [(index, role) for index, role in group if index not in echoed]
+            if not group:
+                return []
+            # ``alternate`` also removed the echoed messages, so it does
+            # not describe this smaller group.
+            return dropped_in(group)
+
+    return dropped_in(group, alternate, have_known=True)
+
+
+def assert_chat_template_rendered_messages(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    chat_template: str,
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+) -> None:
+    """Raise if a non-empty message contributed no prompt content.
+
+    This is a post-condition on chat-template rendering. Roles the template
+    names (``user``, ``assistant``, ``tool``, and template-specific roles)
+    are trusted. Any other role is probed: a unique token is appended to
+    its text and the conversation is rendered again. If the token is absent,
+    the message was dropped and the request is rejected. Tool calls and
+    multimodal parts on that same message are checked too, so echoed text
+    cannot hide a dropped tool call or image. Templates that pass every
+    role through are not probed.
+

+    content to drop, including a tool message that only carries
+    ``tool_call_id``.
+

+        conversation: Messages passed to the template, after rewrites such
+            as developer → system.
+        chat_template: Resolved Jinja source.
+        render_text: Renders a conversation to prompt text with the same
+            template options as the request.
+
+    Raises:
+        VLLMValidationError: A non-empty message produced no prompt
+            content. The error names the role and is returned as HTTP 400.
+
+    """
+    handled = roles_rendered_by_chat_template(chat_template)
+    if handled is None:
+        return
+
+    suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, message in enumerate(conversation)
+        if isinstance((role := message.get("role")), str)
+        and role not in handled
+        and message_has_nonempty_payload(message)
+    ]
+    if not suspects:
+        return
+
+    text_suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, role in suspects
+        if _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("content"))
+        or _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("reasoning"))
+        or _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("reasoning_content"))
+    ]
+    structural_suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, role in suspects
+        if _has_structural_payload(conversation[index])
+    ]
+
+    dropped: list[str] = []
+    if text_suspects:
+        dropped.extend(
+            _roles_dropped_by_text_probe(conversation, text_suspects, render_text)
+        )
+    if structural_suspects:
+        dropped.extend(
+            _roles_dropped_by_omission(
+                conversation,
+                structural_suspects,
+                render_text,
+                strip_payload=True,
+            )
+        )
+    dropped = _unique_roles(dropped)
+    if dropped:
+        raise _unrendered_role_error(dropped)
+
+
+def _roles_dropped_by_text_probe(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    suspects: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+) -> list[str]:
+    try:
+        probed = copy.deepcopy(list(conversation))
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not copy the conversation to check dropped roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return _roles_dropped_by_omission(conversation, suspects, render_text)
+
+    prefix = "vllmprobe" + random_uuid().replace("-", "")[:12]
+    tokens: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
+    for index, role in suspects:
+        token = _role_probe_token(prefix, index)
+        message = probed[index]
+        if isinstance(message, dict) and _inject_probe_token(message, token):
+            tokens.append((token, role))
+    if not tokens:
+        return _roles_dropped_by_omission(conversation, suspects, render_text)
+
+    try:
+        rendered = render_text(probed)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Chat template probe failed while checking role(s) %s.",
+            [role for _, role in suspects],
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return _roles_dropped_by_omission(conversation, suspects, render_text)
+    if not isinstance(rendered, str):
+        return _roles_dropped_by_omission(conversation, suspects, render_text)
+
+    folded = rendered.lower()
+    missing = [role for token, role in tokens if token.lower() not in folded]
+    return missing

🔴 Multi-turn Llama-3.x requests that echo assistant `reasoning` with empty content now get HTTP 400 instead of 200. Tool-call turns are the common case. The text probe treats reasoning as content the template must render. Templates that never render reasoning (or drop old reasoning) lose the token. `missing` then names `assistant` as a dropped role. Fix: inject and check the probe only in `content` text. Treat a missing token as a drop only when that text was absent, and never because unrendered reasoning lost the token.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

examples/tool_chat_template_llama3.1_json.jinja names only 'system', 'ipython' and 'tool' (lines 21, 81, 104), so `handled` excludes 'assistant' and every assistant message becomes a suspect (rendered_roles.py:570). parse_chat_message_content copies client `reasoning` into `reasoning` and `reasoning_content` on assistant messages (chat_message.py:631-634). An assistant turn with `content: null`, a non-empty `reasoning` and `tool_calls` passes `_has_nonempty_text(reasoning)`, so it lands in `text_suspects` (rendered_roles.py:576-582). `_inject_probe_token` puts the token only into reasoning (line 303). The Llama template never emits reasoning, so the token is absent and line 645 reports 'assistant'. `safe_apply_chat_template` (hf.py:845) then raises VLLMValidationError and the client gets HTTP 400. On the base branch the same request rendered and returned 200. The structural path would not flag this turn, but the text-probe result alone is enough to raise.

**Verification:** `_inject_probe_token` (rendered_roles.py:280-308) skips the empty content and appends the token only to `reasoning`/`reasoning_content` (lines 303-307). The template never renders reasoning. The token is absent, so line 645 returns ['assistant']. Line 597 then raises `_unrendered_role_error`, a VLLMValidationError (HTTP 400). On the base these requests returned 200.

</details>

+        token = _role_probe_token(prefix, index)
+        if _stamp_tool_call_probe(message, token):
+            tokens.append((index, token))
+    if not tokens:
+        return set()
+
+    rendered = _render_probe_text(render_text, probed)
+    if rendered is None:
+        return None
+    folded = rendered.lower()
+    return {index for index, token in tokens if token.lower() in folded}
+
+
+def _roles_dropped_by_omission(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    suspects: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+    *,
+    strip_payload: bool = False,
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Roles whose structural payload leaves the rendered prompt unchanged.
+
+    Every suspect is covered by one render. An unchanged prompt means each
+    of them was omitted. If the prompt changes, tool-call names are stamped
+    and checked in a second render so messages the template actually prints
+    are cleared together. Only a mixed remainder is split, and a fully
+    omitted subgroup is still decided by one render.
+
+    When ``strip_payload`` is true, tool calls and multimodal parts are
+    removed but the message stays at the same index. That catches a tool
+    call dropped beside echoed text, and keeps neighbor lookups stable.
+    When false, the whole message is removed. The text-probe fallback uses
+    that to see whether the turn itself was omitted.
+    """
+    try:
+        baseline = render_text(conversation)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not re-render the conversation to check dropped roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return []
+    if not isinstance(baseline, str):
+        logger.warning_once(
+            "Chat template probe did not return text; skipping the dropped-role check."
+        )
+        return []
+
+    group = list(suspects)
+    if not group:
+        return []
+
+    def without(indexes: set[int]) -> list[Mapping[str, Any]]:
+        if strip_payload:
+            return _messages_without_structural_payload(conversation, indexes)
+        return _messages_without(conversation, indexes)
+
+    def dropped_in(
+        subgroup: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+        known_alternate: str | None = None,
+        *,
+        have_known: bool = False,
+    ) -> list[str]:
+        if not subgroup:
+            return []
+        if have_known:
+            alternate = known_alternate
+        else:
+            alternate = _render_probe_text(
+                render_text,
+                without({index for index, _role in subgroup}),
+            )
+        if isinstance(alternate, str) and alternate == baseline:
+            return [role for _index, role in subgroup]
+        # One comparison cannot tell which member of a changed group was
+        # the one that contributed. A single message that changes the
+        # prompt, or whose removal fails to render, is not a silent drop.
+        if len(subgroup) == 1:
+            return []
+        mid = len(subgroup) // 2
+        return dropped_in(subgroup[:mid]) + dropped_in(subgroup[mid:])
+
+    alternate = _render_probe_text(
+        render_text,
+        without({index for index, _role in group}),
+    )
+    if isinstance(alternate, str) and alternate == baseline:
+        return [role for _index, role in group]
+
+    has_tool_calls = False
+    for index, _role in group:
+        message = conversation[index]
+        tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls") if isinstance(message, Mapping) else None
+        if isinstance(tool_calls, list) and tool_calls:
+            has_tool_calls = True
+            break
+    if has_tool_calls:
+        echoed = _tool_call_indexes_echoed(conversation, group, render_text)
+        if echoed:
+            group = [(index, role) for index, role in group if index not in echoed]
+            if not group:
+                return []
+            # ``alternate`` also removed the echoed messages, so it does
+            # not describe this smaller group.
+            return dropped_in(group)
+
+    return dropped_in(group, alternate, have_known=True)
+
+
+def assert_chat_template_rendered_messages(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    chat_template: str,
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+) -> None:
+    """Raise if a non-empty message contributed no prompt content.
+
+    This is a post-condition on chat-template rendering. Roles the template
+    names (``user``, ``assistant``, ``tool``, and template-specific roles)
+    are trusted. Any other role is probed: a unique token is appended to
+    its text and the conversation is rendered again. If the token is absent,
+    the message was dropped and the request is rejected. Tool calls and
+    multimodal parts on that same message are checked too, so echoed text
+    cannot hide a dropped tool call or image. Templates that pass every
+    role through are not probed.
+
+    Empty and whitespace-only messages are not an error. There is no
+    content to drop, including a tool message that only carries
+    ``tool_call_id``.
+
+    Args:
+        conversation: Messages passed to the template, after rewrites such
+            as developer → system.
+        chat_template: Resolved Jinja source.
+        render_text: Renders a conversation to prompt text with the same
+            template options as the request.
+
+    Raises:
+        VLLMValidationError: A non-empty message produced no prompt
+            content. The error names the role and is returned as HTTP 400.
+
+    """
+    handled = roles_rendered_by_chat_template(chat_template)
+    if handled is None:
+        return
+
+    suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, message in enumerate(conversation)
+        if isinstance((role := message.get("role")), str)
+        and role not in handled
+        and message_has_nonempty_payload(message)
+    ]
+    if not suspects:
+        return
+
+    text_suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, role in suspects
+        if _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("content"))
+        or _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("reasoning"))
+        or _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("reasoning_content"))
+    ]
+    structural_suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, role in suspects
+        if _has_structural_payload(conversation[index])
+    ]
+
+    dropped: list[str] = []
+    if text_suspects:
+        dropped.extend(
+            _roles_dropped_by_text_probe(conversation, text_suspects, render_text)
+        )
+    if structural_suspects:
+        dropped.extend(
+            _roles_dropped_by_omission(
+                conversation,
+                structural_suspects,
+                render_text,
+                strip_payload=True,
+            )
+        )
+    dropped = _unique_roles(dropped)
+    if dropped:
+        raise _unrendered_role_error(dropped)
+
+
+def _roles_dropped_by_text_probe(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    suspects: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+) -> list[str]:
+    try:
+        probed = copy.deepcopy(list(conversation))
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not copy the conversation to check dropped roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return _roles_dropped_by_omission(conversation, suspects, render_text)
+
+    prefix = "vllmprobe" + random_uuid().replace("-", "")[:12]
+    tokens: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
+    for index, role in suspects:
+        token = _role_probe_token(prefix, index)
+        message = probed[index]
+        if isinstance(message, dict) and _inject_probe_token(message, token):
+            tokens.append((token, role))
+    if not tokens:
+        return _roles_dropped_by_omission(conversation, suspects, render_text)
+
+    try:
+        rendered = render_text(probed)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Chat template probe failed while checking role(s) %s.",
+            [role for _, role in suspects],
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return _roles_dropped_by_omission(conversation, suspects, render_text)
+    if not isinstance(rendered, str):
+        return _roles_dropped_by_omission(conversation, suspects, render_text)
+
+    folded = rendered.lower()
+    missing = [role for token, role in tokens if token.lower() not in folded]

🔴 Requests that include an ordinary system (or developer) prompt now fail with HTTP 400 on templates that deliberately ignore system turns; the base branch returned 200. Those templates name only 'user'/'assistant', so 'system' is never in `handled`. The text probe then flags it as a dropped turn. The error also tells the caller to "check for a typo in `role`". Fix: reserve the hard 400 for roles outside the standard OpenAI set (system, user, assistant, tool, developer), which is the typo/custom-role case this PR targets. When a template ignores one of those standard roles, log a warning instead of failing the request.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Several bundled templates name only 'user' and 'assistant' and skip every other role. These are vllm/transformers_utils/chat_templates/template_blip2.jinja (lines 2-6), which is the automatic fallback for model_type "blip-2" (registry.py:26, hf.py:304), plus examples/template_falcon.jinja and examples/template_chatglm2.jinja. For these templates roles_rendered_by_chat_template returns {'user','assistant'}. Many clients always prepend {"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."}. That message passes the `role not in handled` and message_has_nonempty_payload filters (rendered_roles.py:570-571), so it becomes a text suspect. The probe token is missing from the render, so _roles_dropped_by_text_probe returns ['system'], and assert_chat_template_rendered_messages raises VLLMValidationError at rendered_roles.py:605. safe_apply_chat_template (hf.py:845) surfaces that as HTTP 400. On the base branch the system prompt was ignored and the request returned 200.

**Verification:** vllm/transformers_utils/chat_templates/template_blip2.jinja has only `message['role'] == 'user'` and `== 'assistant'` (lines 2-6). A system message with text becomes a suspect (rendered_roles.py:566-572). Line 605 then raises `_unrendered_role_error`, which becomes HTTP 400. Nothing exempts standard roles. On the base commit these requests returned 200.

</details>

+    """Append ``token`` to tool-call names this message already has.

+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+) -> set[int] | None:
+    """Suspects whose tool-call name is still present after one probe render.
+
+    ``None`` means the probe did not return text. An empty set means no
+    stamped name showed up; that is not proof the message was dropped.
+    """
+    try:
+        probed = copy.deepcopy(list(conversation))
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not copy the conversation to check dropped roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return None
+
+    prefix = "vllmprobe" + random_uuid().replace("-", "")[:12]
+    tokens: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
+    for index, _role in suspects:
+        message = probed[index]
+        if not isinstance(message, dict):
+            continue
+        token = _role_probe_token(prefix, index)
+        if _stamp_tool_call_probe(message, token):
+            tokens.append((index, token))
+    if not tokens:
+        return set()
+
+    rendered = _render_probe_text(render_text, probed)
+    if rendered is None:
+        return None
+    folded = rendered.lower()
+    return {index for index, token in tokens if token.lower() in folded}
+
+
+def _roles_dropped_by_omission(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    suspects: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+    *,
+    strip_payload: bool = False,
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Roles whose structural payload leaves the rendered prompt unchanged.
+
+    Every suspect is covered by one render. An unchanged prompt means each
+    of them was omitted. If the prompt changes, tool-call names are stamped
+    and checked in a second render so messages the template actually prints
+    are cleared together. Only a mixed remainder is split, and a fully
+    omitted subgroup is still decided by one render.
+
+    When ``strip_payload`` is true, tool calls and multimodal parts are
+    removed but the message stays at the same index. That catches a tool
+    call dropped beside echoed text, and keeps neighbor lookups stable.
+    When false, the whole message is removed. The text-probe fallback uses
+    that to see whether the turn itself was omitted.
+    """
+    try:
+        baseline = render_text(conversation)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not re-render the conversation to check dropped roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return []
+    if not isinstance(baseline, str):
+        logger.warning_once(
+            "Chat template probe did not return text; skipping the dropped-role check."
+        )
+        return []
+
+    group = list(suspects)
+    if not group:
+        return []
+
+    def without(indexes: set[int]) -> list[Mapping[str, Any]]:
+        if strip_payload:
+            return _messages_without_structural_payload(conversation, indexes)
+        return _messages_without(conversation, indexes)
+
+    def dropped_in(
+        subgroup: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+        known_alternate: str | None = None,
+        *,
+        have_known: bool = False,
+    ) -> list[str]:
+        if not subgroup:
+            return []
+        if have_known:
+            alternate = known_alternate
+        else:
+            alternate = _render_probe_text(
+                render_text,
+                without({index for index, _role in subgroup}),
+            )
+        if isinstance(alternate, str) and alternate == baseline:
+            return [role for _index, role in subgroup]
+        # One comparison cannot tell which member of a changed group was
+        # the one that contributed. A single message that changes the
+        # prompt, or whose removal fails to render, is not a silent drop.
+        if len(subgroup) == 1:
+            return []
+        mid = len(subgroup) // 2
+        return dropped_in(subgroup[:mid]) + dropped_in(subgroup[mid:])
+
+    alternate = _render_probe_text(
+        render_text,
+        without({index for index, _role in group}),
+    )
+    if isinstance(alternate, str) and alternate == baseline:
+        return [role for _index, role in group]
+
+    has_tool_calls = False
+    for index, _role in group:
+        message = conversation[index]
+        tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls") if isinstance(message, Mapping) else None
+        if isinstance(tool_calls, list) and tool_calls:
+            has_tool_calls = True
+            break
+    if has_tool_calls:
+        echoed = _tool_call_indexes_echoed(conversation, group, render_text)
+        if echoed:
+            group = [(index, role) for index, role in group if index not in echoed]
+            if not group:
+                return []
+            # ``alternate`` also removed the echoed messages, so it does
+            # not describe this smaller group.
+            return dropped_in(group)
+
+    return dropped_in(group, alternate, have_known=True)
+
+
+def assert_chat_template_rendered_messages(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    chat_template: str,
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+) -> None:
+    """Raise if a non-empty message contributed no prompt content.
+
+    This is a post-condition on chat-template rendering. Roles the template
+    names (``user``, ``assistant``, ``tool``, and template-specific roles)
+    are trusted. Any other role is probed: a unique token is appended to
+    its text and the conversation is rendered again. If the token is absent,
+    the message was dropped and the request is rejected. Tool calls and
+    multimodal parts on that same message are checked too, so echoed text
+    cannot hide a dropped tool call or image. Templates that pass every
+    role through are not probed.
+
+    Empty and whitespace-only messages are not an error. There is no
+    content to drop, including a tool message that only carries
+    ``tool_call_id``.
+
+    Args:
+        conversation: Messages passed to the template, after rewrites such
+            as developer → system.
+        chat_template: Resolved Jinja source.
+        render_text: Renders a conversation to prompt text with the same
+            template options as the request.
+
+    Raises:
+        VLLMValidationError: A non-empty message produced no prompt
+            content. The error names the role and is returned as HTTP 400.
+
+    """
+    handled = roles_rendered_by_chat_template(chat_template)
+    if handled is None:
+        return
+
+    suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, message in enumerate(conversation)
+        if isinstance((role := message.get("role")), str)
+        and role not in handled
+        and message_has_nonempty_payload(message)
+    ]
+    if not suspects:
+        return
+
+    text_suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, role in suspects
+        if _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("content"))
+        or _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("reasoning"))
+        or _has_nonempty_text(conversation[index].get("reasoning_content"))
+    ]
+    structural_suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, role in suspects
+        if _has_structural_payload(conversation[index])
+    ]
+
+    dropped: list[str] = []
+    if text_suspects:
+        dropped.extend(
+            _roles_dropped_by_text_probe(conversation, text_suspects, render_text)
+        )
+    if structural_suspects:
+        dropped.extend(
+            _roles_dropped_by_omission(
+                conversation,
+                structural_suspects,
+                render_text,
+                strip_payload=True,
+            )
+        )
+    dropped = _unique_roles(dropped)
+    if dropped:
+        raise _unrendered_role_error(dropped)

🟡 (optional) Ordinary chat requests on Llama-3.x-style templates now pay a deep copy and a second full template render on every request. Those templates only compare `system`/`tool`/`ipython`, so plain `user` and `assistant` turns always count as suspects. That makes the new check run on the hot path even when every role renders. Fix: also treat a template as rendering a role when it outputs the role dynamically (e.g. `{{ message['role'] }}` in the branch that unknown roles reach). Alternatively, skip the probe when the first render already contains each suspect's text, so valid requests need no extra render. [also at: vllm/renderers/chat_utils/rendered_roles.py:211 - Ordinary user and assistant chats on some catch-all templates now pay 1–4 extra full template renders per request; on the base branch each request renders once.]

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

examples/tool_chat_template_llama3.1_json.jinja (lines 21, 81, 104) compares role only to 'system', 'ipython' and 'tool', and renders user and assistant through `message['role']` at line 82. `roles_rendered_by_chat_template` therefore returns {'system','ipython','tool'}, and every non-empty user or assistant message is a suspect (rendered_roles.py:570). `assert_chat_template_rendered_messages` then calls `_roles_dropped_by_text_probe`, which deep-copies the conversation and calls `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` again through the lambda at hf.py:848. This happens on every /v1/chat/completions request for these models, even when nothing is dropped. On the base branch the template rendered once per request. The PR description says valid requests are unchanged, but for these widely used templates each request now costs one extra full render plus a conversation copy. The `lru_cache` covers only the AST parse, not the render.

**Verification:** Trigger: any chat request whose template compares `role` against only a subset of the standard roles, as Llama-3.1/3.2/3.3-style templates do. At rendered_roles.py:566-572, every non-empty `user` and `assistant` message is a suspect, so `_roles_dropped_by_text_probe` runs a second full `render_text(probed)` (l.633). The base commit has no such re-render.

</details>

🔴 Clients sending OpenAI's legacy `function` role now get HTTP 400 on templates that ignore it. Other OpenAI roles only log a warning there. `_STANDARD_CHAT_ROLES` lists system, user, assistant, tool and developer, but not `function`. So a non-empty function message is treated like a typo and goes through the hard-error path at rendered_roles.py:980. Fix: make the standard-role set match every role the request schema accepts (OpenAI's chat message union, which includes `function`). Each role in that union should then warn instead of raising, the same way `tool` does.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The request schema accepts `OpenAIChatCompletionMessageParam` (vllm/renderers/chat_utils/types.py:314). That union includes OpenAI's deprecated function message, `{"role": "function", "name": ..., "content": "result"}`, which older agent clients still send. Some templates name role literals and never print `message.role` for other roles. Examples are Qwen2.5-style if-chains over user/system/assistant/tool and `template_blip2.jinja`. On those templates the function message counts as a suspect at rendered_roles.py:955-962. It lands in `hard` because `function` is not in `_STANDARD_CHAT_ROLES` (line 49, filtered at 968-970). The text probe finds no token, and line 980 raises `_unrendered_role_error`, which reaches the client from `safe_apply_chat_template` (hf.py:846) as HTTP 400 with the message "check for a typo in `role`". On the base branch the same request returned 200. The PR's stated policy is that a standard OpenAI role the template ignores is only logged, and that policy does not cover this spec role.

**Verification:** Trigger: a client sends a non-empty legacy `{"role": "function", ...}` message to a model whose template never prints it, such as template_blip2.jinja (lines 2-6). `_STANDARD_CHAT_ROLES` (rendered_roles.py:47-49) leaves out `function`, so line 969 puts it in `hard`, not the warn-only `soft` list, and line 980 raises `_unrendered_role_error` as HTTP 400. On the base branch the same request returned 200.

</details>

🟡 (optional) Typo-role turns can still vanish with HTTP 200 when a template prints the role header for every message but prints content only for named roles. A role is skipped from probing whenever any role-printing path is unconstrained (`passes_unlisted`). Content paths are ignored in that decision. Fix: trust an unlisted role only when some content path also allows it. Probe it otherwise. `_template_role_emission` already returns `content_paths`, and `_constraint_allows_role` can check them.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Take a template like `{% for message in messages %}<|{{ message['role'] }}|>{% if message['role'] == 'user' %}{{ message['content'] }}{% elif message['role'] == 'assistant' %}{{ message['content'] }}{% endif %}{% endfor %}` and a /v1/chat/completions request whose message has role "usr" and non-empty content. The request reaches assert_chat_template_rendered_messages via safe_apply_chat_template (vllm/renderers/hf.py:846). `_template_role_emission` (rendered_roles.py:556-568) records the header output as an unconstrained role path. It returns passes_unlisted=True with excluded=frozenset(). The filter at rendered_roles.py:960, `not (passes_unlisted and role not in excluded)`, then removes "usr" from the suspects without any probe render. The prompt ends up as `<|usr|>` with the content missing, and the request returns 200. That is exactly the silent drop this PR says it rejects with 400. The content_paths list computed in the same function shows only fixed {user} and {assistant} content paths, but the suspect filter never consults it.

**Verification:** nit (pre-existing: the base also returns 200 with the turn dropped). Trigger: a chat template prints `message['role']` with no guard but prints `message['content']` only inside named-role branches, and the request uses a typo or custom role. At rendered_roles.py:960, `and not (passes_unlisted and role not in excluded)` is False for 'usr', so the message is never a suspect.

</details>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import copy
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
+from functools import lru_cache
+from typing import Any, Literal, NamedTuple
+
+import jinja2.ext
+import jinja2.nodes
+import jinja2.parser
+import jinja2.sandbox
+
+from vllm.exceptions import VLLMValidationError
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.utils import random_uuid
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class _ChatTemplateParseExtension(jinja2.ext.Extension):
+    """Accept HF ``{% generation %}`` blocks while parsing a chat template."""
+
+    tags = {"generation"}
+
+    def parse(self, parser: jinja2.parser.Parser) -> jinja2.nodes.Node:
+        lineno = next(parser.stream).lineno
+        body = parser.parse_statements(("name:endgeneration",), drop_needle=True)
+        return jinja2.nodes.Scope(body).set_lineno(lineno)
+
+
+# Same sandbox + loop/generation extensions used when a template is rendered.
+_CHAT_TEMPLATE_JINJA_ENV = jinja2.sandbox.ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment(
+    trim_blocks=True,
+    lstrip_blocks=True,
+    extensions=[_ChatTemplateParseExtension, jinja2.ext.loopcontrols],
+)
+_TEXT_PART_TYPES = frozenset(
+    {
+        "text",
+        "input_text",
+        "output_text",
+        "refusal",
+        "thinking",
+    }
+)
+# OpenAI chat roles. A template may ignore these on purpose; a typo or a
+# custom role is outside this set and can still be a hard error.
+_STANDARD_CHAT_ROLES = frozenset({"system", "user", "assistant", "tool", "developer"})
+
+
+def _is_role_access(node: jinja2.nodes.Node) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``node`` reads ``.role`` or ``['role']``."""
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Getattr):
+        return node.attr == "role"
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Getitem):
+        return isinstance(node.arg, jinja2.nodes.Const) and node.arg.value == "role"
+    return False
+
+
+def _literal_role_names(node: jinja2.nodes.Node) -> list[str] | None:
+    """String literal, or a list/tuple of them. ``None`` if not pure literals."""
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Const) and isinstance(node.value, str):
+        return [node.value]
+    if isinstance(node, (jinja2.nodes.List, jinja2.nodes.Tuple)):
+        names: list[str] = []
+        for item in node.items:
+            if not isinstance(item, jinja2.nodes.Const) or not isinstance(
+                item.value, str
+            ):
+                return None
+            names.append(item.value)
+        return names
+    return None
+
+
+# Inclusion tests passed to selectattr/rejectattr. Exclusion tests (``ne``)
+# and rejectattr do not name roles the template keeps.
+_ROLE_INCLUDE_TESTS = frozenset({"equalto", "eq", "==", "sameas", "in"})
+
+
+def _roles_from_attr_filter(
+    node: jinja2.nodes.Filter,
+) -> tuple[Literal["ignore", "literal", "dynamic"], set[str]]:
+    """Classify a ``selectattr`` / ``rejectattr`` call on ``role``.
+
+    ``selectattr('role', 'equalto', 'user')`` keeps that literal role.
+    ``rejectattr``, a non-literal target, or a test that is not an
+    inclusion (``ne``) still means the template filters by role, but the
+    kept names are not a literal allow-list.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``("ignore", empty)`` when the filter does not test ``role``,
+        ``("literal", names)`` when ``selectattr`` names kept roles, or
+        ``("dynamic", empty)`` when the filter is real but the kept
+        roles are not literals.
+
+    """
+    if node.name not in {"selectattr", "rejectattr"} or not node.args:
+        return "ignore", set()
+    attr = node.args[0]
+    if not isinstance(attr, jinja2.nodes.Const) or attr.value != "role":
+        return "ignore", set()
+    if node.name != "selectattr" or len(node.args) < 3:
+        return "dynamic", set()
+    test = node.args[1]
+    if (
+        not isinstance(test, jinja2.nodes.Const)
+        or test.value not in _ROLE_INCLUDE_TESTS
+    ):
+        return "dynamic", set()
+    names = _literal_role_names(node.args[2])
+    if names is None:
+        return "dynamic", set()
+    return "literal", set(names)
+
+
+def _roles_from_compare(
+    node: jinja2.nodes.Compare,
+) -> tuple[Literal["ignore", "literal", "dynamic"], set[str]]:
+    """Classify one comparison that might select rendered roles.
+
+    Only ``==`` and ``in`` count. ``!=`` and ``not in`` are generation-prompt
+    guards (ChatML checks ``messages[-1]['role'] != 'assistant'``) and do not
+    select which roles are rendered. A non-literal target, whether
+    ``message.role in allowed_roles`` or ``message.role == some_var``, is
+    dynamic.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``("ignore", empty)`` when the node is not a role inclusion test,
+        ``("literal", names)`` when the accepted roles are string literals
+        (an empty list is a literal filter that names nothing), or
+        ``("dynamic", empty)`` when the allow-list is not a literal.
+
+    """
+    if not node.ops:
+        return "ignore", set()
+    # Chained comparisons compare later operands with each other, not with
+    # the role expression.
+    operand = node.ops[0]
+    op = operand.op
+    if op not in {"eq", "in"}:
+        return "ignore", set()
+
+    left_is_role = _is_role_access(node.expr)
+    right_is_role = _is_role_access(operand.expr)
+    if op == "eq":
+        if not left_is_role and not right_is_role:
+            return "ignore", set()
+        literal_node = operand.expr if left_is_role else node.expr
+        names = _literal_role_names(literal_node)
+        if names is None:
+            # ``message.role == some_var`` names no literal. Same as
+            # ``role in allowed_roles``: a filter may exist, so probe
+            # instead of skipping the check.
+            return "dynamic", set()
+        return "literal", set(names)
+
+    if not left_is_role:
+        return "ignore", set()
+    names = _literal_role_names(operand.expr)
+    if names is None:
+        return "dynamic", set()
+    return "literal", set(names)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
+def roles_rendered_by_chat_template(chat_template: str) -> frozenset[str] | None:
+    """Return roles a template explicitly dispatches on.
+
+    The Jinja AST is walked for comparisons that read ``.role`` or
+    ``['role']``, and for ``selectattr`` / ``rejectattr`` on ``role``.
+    ``None`` means the template does not filter by role, so every role is
+    emitted (ChatML-style ``{{ message['role'] }}``). A frozenset, possibly
+    empty, means unknown roles can be dropped and must be checked after
+    render.
+
+    Args:
+        chat_template: Resolved Jinja source.
+
+    Returns:
+        Roles named by ``==`` / ``in`` tests or by ``selectattr`` on
+        ``role``. An empty set means the template filters on role, but the
+        allowed names are not literals (``message.role in allowed_roles``,
+        ``message.role == some_var``, or ``rejectattr``). ``None`` means
+        there is no role filter.
+
+    """
+    try:
+        parsed = _CHAT_TEMPLATE_JINJA_ENV.parse(chat_template)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not parse the chat template while checking message roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return None
+
+    roles: set[str] = set()
+    saw_role_filter = False
+    findings = [
+        _roles_from_compare(node) for node in parsed.find_all(jinja2.nodes.Compare)
+    ]
+    findings.extend(
+        _roles_from_attr_filter(node) for node in parsed.find_all(jinja2.nodes.Filter)
+    )
+    for kind, found in findings:
+        if kind == "ignore":
+            continue
+        saw_role_filter = True
+        if kind == "literal":
+            roles.update(found)
+    if not saw_role_filter:
+        return None
+    return frozenset(roles)
+
+
+class _RoleConstraint(NamedTuple):
+    """How one template path limits ``message.role``.
+
+    ``roles is None`` means the path does not pin the role to literals.
+    ``excludes`` means the role must fall outside ``roles``.
+    """
+
+    roles: frozenset[str] | None
+    excludes: bool
+
+
+def _any_role() -> _RoleConstraint:
+    return _RoleConstraint(None, False)
+
+
+def _fixed_roles(names: Iterable[str]) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    return _RoleConstraint(frozenset(names), False)
+
+
+def _excluded_roles(names: Iterable[str]) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    return _RoleConstraint(frozenset(names), True)
+
+
+def _and_role_constraints(
+    left: _RoleConstraint, right: _RoleConstraint
+) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    if left.roles is None and not left.excludes:
+        return right
+    if right.roles is None and not right.excludes:
+        return left
+    left_roles = left.roles or frozenset()
+    right_roles = right.roles or frozenset()
+    if not left.excludes and not right.excludes:
+        return _fixed_roles(left_roles & right_roles)
+    if left.excludes and right.excludes:
+        return _excluded_roles(left_roles | right_roles)
+    fixed = left_roles if not left.excludes else right_roles
+    excluded = right_roles if not left.excludes else left_roles
+    return _fixed_roles(fixed - excluded)
+
+
+def _or_role_constraints(
+    left: _RoleConstraint, right: _RoleConstraint
+) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    if (left.roles is None and not left.excludes) or (
+        right.roles is None and not right.excludes
+    ):
+        return _any_role()
+    left_roles = left.roles or frozenset()
+    right_roles = right.roles or frozenset()
+    if not left.excludes and not right.excludes:
+        return _fixed_roles(left_roles | right_roles)
+    if left.excludes and right.excludes:
+        return _excluded_roles(left_roles & right_roles)
+    fixed = left_roles if not left.excludes else right_roles
+    excluded = right_roles if not left.excludes else left_roles
+    return _excluded_roles(excluded - fixed)
+
+
+def _not_role_constraint(constraint: _RoleConstraint) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    if constraint.roles is None:
+        return _any_role()
+    if not constraint.excludes:
+        return _excluded_roles(constraint.roles)
+    return _fixed_roles(constraint.roles)
+
+
+def _is_field_access(node: jinja2.nodes.Node, field: str) -> bool:
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Getattr):
+        return node.attr == field
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Getitem):
+        return isinstance(node.arg, jinja2.nodes.Const) and node.arg.value == field
+    return False
+
+
+def _field_base_name(node: jinja2.nodes.Node) -> str | None:
+    base = node.node  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+    if isinstance(base, jinja2.nodes.Name):
+        return base.name
+    return None
+
+
+def _role_vars_in(expr: jinja2.nodes.Node) -> set[str]:
+    found: set[str] = set()
+
+    def walk(node: jinja2.nodes.Node) -> None:
+        if _is_field_access(node, "role"):
+            base = _field_base_name(node)
+            if base:
+                found.add(base)
+        for child in node.iter_child_nodes():
+            walk(child)
+
+    walk(expr)
+    return found
+
+
+def _compare_role_constraint(node: jinja2.nodes.Compare, var: str) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    if not node.ops:
+        return _any_role()
+    operand = node.ops[0]
+
+    def role_var(expr: jinja2.nodes.Node) -> str | None:
+        if _is_field_access(expr, "role"):
+            return _field_base_name(expr)
+        return None
+
+    left = role_var(node.expr)
+    right = role_var(operand.expr)
+    op = operand.op
+    if op in {"eq", "ne"}:
+        if left != var and right != var:
+            return _any_role()
+        literal = operand.expr if left == var else node.expr
+        names = _literal_role_names(literal)
+        if names is None:
+            return _any_role()
+        if op == "eq":
+            return _fixed_roles(names)
+        return _excluded_roles(names)
+    if op in {"in", "notin"} and left == var:
+        names = _literal_role_names(operand.expr)
+        if names is None:
+            return _any_role()
+        if op == "in":
+            return _fixed_roles(names)
+        return _excluded_roles(names)
+    return _any_role()
+
+
+def _constraint_on_var(expr: jinja2.nodes.Node, var: str) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    if isinstance(expr, jinja2.nodes.And):
+        return _and_role_constraints(
+            _constraint_on_var(expr.left, var),
+            _constraint_on_var(expr.right, var),
+        )
+    if isinstance(expr, jinja2.nodes.Or):
+        return _or_role_constraints(
+            _constraint_on_var(expr.left, var),
+            _constraint_on_var(expr.right, var),
+        )
+    if isinstance(expr, jinja2.nodes.Not):
+        return _not_role_constraint(_constraint_on_var(expr.node, var))
+    if isinstance(expr, jinja2.nodes.Compare):
+        return _compare_role_constraint(expr, var)
+    return _any_role()
+
+
+def _filter_role_constraint(node: jinja2.nodes.Filter) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    if node.name not in {"selectattr", "rejectattr"} or not node.args:
+        return _any_role()
+    attr = node.args[0]
+    if not isinstance(attr, jinja2.nodes.Const) or attr.value != "role":
+        return _any_role()
+    if len(node.args) < 3:
+        return _any_role()
+    test = node.args[1]
+    if (
+        not isinstance(test, jinja2.nodes.Const)
+        or test.value not in _ROLE_INCLUDE_TESTS
+    ):
+        return _any_role()
+    names = _literal_role_names(node.args[2])
+    if names is None:
+        return _any_role()
+    if node.name == "rejectattr":
+        return _excluded_roles(names)
+    return _fixed_roles(names)
+
+
+def _iterator_role_constraint(node: jinja2.nodes.Node) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Filter):
+        return _and_role_constraints(
+            _iterator_role_constraint(node.node),
+            _filter_role_constraint(node),
+        )
+    return _any_role()
+
+
+def _merged_role_constraint(
+    var: str,
+    bindings: Mapping[str, _RoleConstraint],
+    guards: Sequence[tuple[str, _RoleConstraint]],
+) -> _RoleConstraint:
+    constraint = bindings.get(var, _any_role())
+    for guard_var, guard in guards:
+        if guard_var == var:
+            constraint = _and_role_constraints(constraint, guard)
+    return constraint
+
+
+def _collect_output_fields(
+    expr: jinja2.nodes.Node,
+    bindings: Mapping[str, _RoleConstraint],
+    guards: Sequence[tuple[str, _RoleConstraint]],
+    role_paths: list[_RoleConstraint],
+    content_paths: list[_RoleConstraint],
+) -> None:
+    if isinstance(expr, jinja2.nodes.CondExpr):
+        mentioned = _role_vars_in(expr.test)
+        true_guards = [
+            *guards,
+            *[(var, _constraint_on_var(expr.test, var)) for var in mentioned],
+        ]
+        false_guards = [
+            *guards,
+            *[
+                (var, _not_role_constraint(_constraint_on_var(expr.test, var)))
+                for var in mentioned
+            ],
+        ]
+        _collect_output_fields(
+            expr.expr1, bindings, true_guards, role_paths, content_paths
+        )
+        if expr.expr2 is not None:
+            _collect_output_fields(
+                expr.expr2, bindings, false_guards, role_paths, content_paths
+            )
+        return
+    if _is_field_access(expr, "role"):
+        base = _field_base_name(expr)
+        if base:
+            role_paths.append(_merged_role_constraint(base, bindings, guards))
+    if _is_field_access(expr, "content"):
+        base = _field_base_name(expr)
+        if base:
+            content_paths.append(_merged_role_constraint(base, bindings, guards))
+    for child in expr.iter_child_nodes():
+        _collect_output_fields(child, bindings, guards, role_paths, content_paths)
+
+
+def _walk_guarded_stmts(
+    nodes: Iterable[jinja2.nodes.Node],
+    bindings: Mapping[str, _RoleConstraint],
+    guards: Sequence[tuple[str, _RoleConstraint]],
+    role_paths: list[_RoleConstraint],
+    content_paths: list[_RoleConstraint],
+) -> None:
+    for node in nodes:
+        _walk_template_node(node, bindings, role_paths, content_paths, guards)
+
+
+def _walk_template_node(
+    node: jinja2.nodes.Node,
+    bindings: Mapping[str, _RoleConstraint],
+    role_paths: list[_RoleConstraint],
+    content_paths: list[_RoleConstraint],
+    guards: Sequence[tuple[str, _RoleConstraint]] = (),
+) -> None:
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.If):
+        _walk_if_chain(node, bindings, role_paths, content_paths, guards)
+        return
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.For):
+        new_bindings = bindings
+        if isinstance(node.target, jinja2.nodes.Name):
+            var = node.target.name
+            constraint = _iterator_role_constraint(node.iter)
+            if node.test is not None:
+                constraint = _and_role_constraints(
+                    constraint, _constraint_on_var(node.test, var)
+                )
+            constraint = _and_role_constraints(
+                bindings.get(var, _any_role()), constraint
+            )
+            new_bindings = {**bindings, var: constraint}
+        _walk_guarded_stmts(node.body, new_bindings, guards, role_paths, content_paths)
+        _walk_guarded_stmts(node.else_, bindings, guards, role_paths, content_paths)
+        return
+    if isinstance(node, jinja2.nodes.Output):
+        for expr in node.nodes:
+            _collect_output_fields(expr, bindings, guards, role_paths, content_paths)
+        return
+    for child in node.iter_child_nodes():
+        if isinstance(child, jinja2.nodes.Stmt):
+            _walk_template_node(child, bindings, role_paths, content_paths, guards)
+
+
+def _walk_if_chain(
+    node: jinja2.nodes.If,
+    bindings: Mapping[str, _RoleConstraint],
+    role_paths: list[_RoleConstraint],
+    content_paths: list[_RoleConstraint],
+    outer_guards: Sequence[tuple[str, _RoleConstraint]] = (),
+) -> None:
+    """Walk an if/elif/else chain, keeping earlier failed tests."""
+    pending: list[tuple[str, _RoleConstraint]] = list(outer_guards)
+    for branch in (node, *node.elif_):
+        mentioned = _role_vars_in(branch.test)
+        passed = pending + [
+            (var, _constraint_on_var(branch.test, var)) for var in mentioned
+        ]
+        _walk_guarded_stmts(branch.body, bindings, passed, role_paths, content_paths)
+        pending = pending + [
+            (var, _not_role_constraint(_constraint_on_var(branch.test, var)))
+            for var in mentioned
+        ]
+    _walk_guarded_stmts(node.else_, bindings, pending, role_paths, content_paths)
+
+
+def _constraint_passes_unlisted(constraint: _RoleConstraint) -> bool:
+    return constraint.roles is None or constraint.excludes
+
+
+def _constraint_allows_role(constraint: _RoleConstraint, role: str) -> bool:
+    if constraint.roles is None:
+        return True
+    if constraint.excludes:
+        return role not in constraint.roles
+    return role in constraint.roles
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
+def _template_role_emission(
+    chat_template: str,
+) -> tuple[bool, frozenset[str], tuple[_RoleConstraint, ...]]:
+    """How a template prints roles, and which content paths exist.
+
+    Returns:
+        ``passes_unlisted`` is true when some output prints
+        ``message['role']`` on a path that is not limited to the literal
+        roles the template compares. ``excluded`` is the roles that cannot
+        reach any such output. ``content_paths`` are the role constraints
+        on outputs that read message content.
+
+    """
+    try:
+        parsed = _CHAT_TEMPLATE_JINJA_ENV.parse(chat_template)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not parse the chat template while checking message roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return False, frozenset(), ()
+
+    role_paths: list[_RoleConstraint] = []
+    content_paths: list[_RoleConstraint] = []
+    _walk_guarded_stmts(parsed.body, {}, (), role_paths, content_paths)
+
+    exclusions: list[frozenset[str]] = []
+    for constraint in role_paths:
+        if not _constraint_passes_unlisted(constraint):
+            continue
+        if constraint.excludes and constraint.roles is not None:
+            exclusions.append(constraint.roles)
+        else:
+            exclusions.append(frozenset())
+    if not exclusions:
+        return False, frozenset(), tuple(content_paths)
+    excluded = exclusions[0]
+    for item in exclusions[1:]:
+        excluded &= item
+    return True, excluded, tuple(content_paths)
+
+
+def _has_nonempty_text(value: Any) -> bool:
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        return bool(value.strip())
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return _has_nonempty_text(value.get("text"))
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return any(_has_nonempty_text(part) for part in value)
+    return False
+
+
+def message_has_nonempty_payload(message: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    """Whether a message carries content the template must not drop.
+
+    Empty and whitespace-only text is not a payload. Templates may omit
+    those turns, and there is no user-visible content to lose. A tool-call
+    id with no arguments or result text is treated the same way. Multimodal
+    parts and tool calls are payloads even when they have no text.
+    """
+    if _has_nonempty_text(message.get("content")):
+        return True
+    if _has_nonempty_text(message.get("reasoning")):
+        return True
+    if _has_nonempty_text(message.get("reasoning_content")):
+        return True
+    return _has_structural_payload(message)
+
+
+def _has_structural_payload(message: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    """Whether a message carries tool calls or non-text multimodal parts."""
+    tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls")
+    if isinstance(tool_calls, list) and len(tool_calls) > 0:
+        return True
+    content = message.get("content")
+    if isinstance(content, list):
+        for part in content:
+            if isinstance(part, dict):
+                part_type = part.get("type")
+                if part_type not in _TEXT_PART_TYPES and part_type is not None:
+                    return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _strip_structural_payload(message: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Copy ``message`` without tool calls or multimodal parts.
+
+    Text stays, and the message keeps its index. Removing the whole turn
+    would hide a dropped tool call behind echoed text, and would also shift
+    later messages in templates that read neighbors by position.
+    """
+    updated = dict(message)
+    tool_calls = updated.get("tool_calls")
+    if isinstance(tool_calls, list) and tool_calls:
+        updated["tool_calls"] = []
+    content = updated.get("content")
+    if isinstance(content, list):
+        kept: list[Any] = []
+        for part in content:
+            if isinstance(part, dict):
+                part_type = part.get("type")
+                if part_type not in _TEXT_PART_TYPES and part_type is not None:
+                    continue
+            kept.append(part)
+        updated["content"] = kept
+    return updated
+
+
+def _inject_probe_token(message: dict[str, Any], token: str) -> bool:
+    """Append ``token`` to content text so a render can prove inclusion.
+
+    Reasoning is not probed. Templates often keep it out of the prompt, and
+    a missing reasoning string is not a dropped turn.
+    """
+    injected = False
+    content = message.get("content")
+    if isinstance(content, str) and content.strip():
+        message["content"] = content + token
+        injected = True
+    elif isinstance(content, list):
+        parts: list[Any] = []
+        for part in content:
+            if isinstance(part, str) and part.strip():
+                parts.append(part + token)
+                injected = True
+            elif isinstance(part, dict):
+                updated = dict(part)
+                text = updated.get("text")
+                if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip():
+                    updated["text"] = text + token
+                    injected = True
+                parts.append(updated)
+            else:
+                parts.append(part)
+        message["content"] = parts
+    return injected
+
+
+def _warn_ignored_standard_roles(roles: Sequence[str]) -> None:
+    """Log once when a template ignores a standard chat role."""
+    shown = tuple(_unique_roles(roles))
+    if not shown:
+        return
+    logger.warning_once(
+        "Chat template produced no prompt content for non-empty "
+        "standard message role(s) %s. The request is still accepted; "
+        "this template does not render that role.",
+        shown,
+    )
+
+
+def _unrendered_role_error(roles: list[str]) -> VLLMValidationError:
+    shown = ", ".join(repr(role) for role in roles)
+    noun = "role" if len(roles) == 1 else "roles"
+    return VLLMValidationError(
+        "Chat template produced no prompt content for non-empty "
+        f"message {noun} {shown}. The template did not emit that "
+        "content, so the turn would be dropped. Custom roles are "
+        "accepted when the template renders their content; check for "
+        "a typo in `role`.",
+        parameter="messages",
+        value=roles[0] if len(roles) == 1 else roles,
+    )
+
+
+def _unique_roles(roles: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:
+    seen: list[str] = []
+    for role in roles:
+        if role not in seen:
+            seen.append(role)
+    return seen
+
+
+def _role_probe_token(prefix: str, index: int) -> str:
+    """Build a probe token that is not a substring of another index's token."""
+    return f"{prefix}_{index:06d}_"
+
+
+def _render_probe_text(
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+    messages: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+) -> str | None:
+    try:
+        rendered = render_text(messages)
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+    if not isinstance(rendered, str):
+        return None
+    return rendered
+
+
+def _messages_without(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    indexes: set[int],
+) -> list[Mapping[str, Any]]:
+    return [
+        message for index, message in enumerate(conversation) if index not in indexes
+    ]
+
+
+def _messages_without_structural_payload(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    indexes: set[int],
+) -> list[Mapping[str, Any]]:
+    return [
+        _strip_structural_payload(message) if index in indexes else message
+        for index, message in enumerate(conversation)
+    ]
+
+
+def _stamp_tool_call_probe(message: dict[str, Any], token: str) -> bool:
+    """Append ``token`` to tool-call names this message already has.
+
+    A new text part is not added. A template can echo that part while still
+    dropping the tool call or image that made the message a suspect.
+    """
+    tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls")
+    if not isinstance(tool_calls, list):
+        return False
+    stamped: list[Any] = []
+    wrote = False
+    for call in tool_calls:
+        if not isinstance(call, dict):
+            stamped.append(call)
+            continue
+        call = copy.deepcopy(call)
+        function = call.get("function")
+        if isinstance(function, dict) and isinstance(function.get("name"), str):
+            function["name"] = function["name"] + token
+            wrote = True
+        stamped.append(call)
+    if wrote:
+        message["tool_calls"] = stamped
+    return wrote
+
+
+def _tool_call_indexes_echoed(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    suspects: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+) -> set[int] | None:
+    """Suspects whose tool-call name is still present after one probe render.
+
+    ``None`` means the probe did not return text. An empty set means no
+    stamped name showed up; that is not proof the message was dropped.
+    """
+    try:
+        probed = copy.deepcopy(list(conversation))
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not copy the conversation to check dropped roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return None
+
+    prefix = "vllmprobe" + random_uuid().replace("-", "")[:12]
+    tokens: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
+    for index, _role in suspects:
+        message = probed[index]
+        if not isinstance(message, dict):
+            continue
+        token = _role_probe_token(prefix, index)
+        if _stamp_tool_call_probe(message, token):
+            tokens.append((index, token))
+    if not tokens:
+        return set()
+
+    rendered = _render_probe_text(render_text, probed)
+    if rendered is None:
+        return None
+    folded = rendered.lower()
+    return {index for index, token in tokens if token.lower() in folded}
+
+
+def _indexes_dropped_by_omission(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    suspects: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+    *,
+    strip_payload: bool = False,
+) -> set[int]:
+    """Indexes whose structural payload leaves the rendered prompt unchanged.
+
+    Every suspect is covered by one render. An unchanged prompt means each
+    of them was omitted. If the prompt changes, tool-call names are stamped
+    and checked in a second render so messages the template actually prints
+    are cleared together. Only a mixed remainder is split, and a fully
+    omitted subgroup is still decided by one render.
+
+    When ``strip_payload`` is true, tool calls and multimodal parts are
+    removed but the message stays at the same index. That catches a tool
+    call dropped beside echoed text, and keeps neighbor lookups stable.
+    When false, the whole message is removed. The text-probe fallback uses
+    that to see whether the turn itself was omitted.
+    """
+    try:
+        baseline = render_text(conversation)
+    except Exception:
+        logger.warning(
+            "Could not re-render the conversation to check dropped roles.",
+            exc_info=True,
+        )
+        return set()
+    if not isinstance(baseline, str):
+        logger.warning_once(
+            "Chat template probe did not return text; skipping the dropped-role check."
+        )
+        return set()
+
+    group = list(suspects)
+    if not group:
+        return set()
+
+    def without(indexes: set[int]) -> list[Mapping[str, Any]]:
+        if strip_payload:
+            return _messages_without_structural_payload(conversation, indexes)
+        return _messages_without(conversation, indexes)
+
+    def dropped_in(
+        subgroup: Sequence[tuple[int, str]],
+        known_alternate: str | None = None,
+        *,
+        have_known: bool = False,
+    ) -> set[int]:
+        if not subgroup:
+            return set()
+        if have_known:
+            alternate = known_alternate
+        else:
+            alternate = _render_probe_text(
+                render_text,
+                without({index for index, _role in subgroup}),
+            )
+        if isinstance(alternate, str) and alternate == baseline:
+            return {index for index, _role in subgroup}
+        # One comparison cannot tell which member of a changed group was
+        # the one that contributed. A single message that changes the
+        # prompt, or whose removal fails to render, is not a silent drop.
+        if len(subgroup) == 1:
+            return set()
+        mid = len(subgroup) // 2
+        return dropped_in(subgroup[:mid]) | dropped_in(subgroup[mid:])
+
+    alternate = _render_probe_text(
+        render_text,
+        without({index for index, _role in group}),
+    )
+    if isinstance(alternate, str) and alternate == baseline:
+        return {index for index, _role in group}
+
+    has_tool_calls = False
+    for index, _role in group:
+        message = conversation[index]
+        tool_calls = message.get("tool_calls") if isinstance(message, Mapping) else None
+        if isinstance(tool_calls, list) and tool_calls:
+            has_tool_calls = True
+            break
+    if has_tool_calls:
+        echoed = _tool_call_indexes_echoed(conversation, group, render_text)
+        if echoed:
+            group = [(index, role) for index, role in group if index not in echoed]
+            if not group:
+                return set()
+            # ``alternate`` also removed the echoed messages, so it does
+            # not describe this smaller group.
+            return dropped_in(group)
+
+    return dropped_in(group, alternate, have_known=True)
+
+
+def _ignored_standard_roles(
+    roles: Sequence[str],
+    content_paths: Sequence[_RoleConstraint],
+    handled: frozenset[str],
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Standard roles the template can be shown to skip, without re-rendering."""
+    ignored: list[str] = []
+    for role in _unique_roles(roles):
+        if content_paths:
+            if any(_constraint_allows_role(path, role) for path in content_paths):
+                continue
+            ignored.append(role)
+        elif handled and role not in handled:
+            ignored.append(role)
+    return ignored
+
+
+def assert_chat_template_rendered_messages(
+    conversation: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
+    chat_template: str,
+    render_text: Callable[[Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]], str],
+) -> None:
+    """Raise if a non-empty message contributed no prompt content.
+
+    This is a post-condition on chat-template rendering. Roles the template
+    names are trusted. So is a role printed with ``message['role']`` on a
+    path that is not limited to those names. Any other non-standard role is
+    probed: a unique token is appended to its content and the conversation
+    is rendered again. The turn is rejected only when it adds nothing to
+    the prompt. A rendered tool call or image keeps the turn, and echoed
+    text does not hide a dropped tool call or image.
+
+    Standard roles (``system``, ``user``, ``assistant``, ``tool``,
+    ``developer``) are not rejected. When the template ignores one, a
+    warning is logged and the request continues. That path does not copy
+    the conversation or render it again. Empty and whitespace-only messages
+    are not an error.
+
+    Args:
+        conversation: Messages passed to the template, after rewrites such
+            as developer → system.
+        chat_template: Resolved Jinja source.
+        render_text: Renders a conversation to prompt text with the same
+            template options as the request.
+
+    Raises:
+        VLLMValidationError: A non-empty non-standard message produced no
+            prompt content. The error names the role and is returned as
+            HTTP 400.
+
+    """
+    handled = roles_rendered_by_chat_template(chat_template)
+    if handled is None:
+        return
+
+    passes_unlisted, excluded, content_paths = _template_role_emission(chat_template)
+    suspects = [
+        (index, role)
+        for index, message in enumerate(conversation)
+        if isinstance((role := message.get("role")), str)
+        and role not in handled
+        and not (passes_unlisted and role not in excluded)
